title: Smooth algebraic spaces have base-change compatible relative dimension strata
statement:
Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X	o B$ be a morphism from an algebraic space $X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], smooth on etale scheme charts in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Use the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], open subspaces [def-a1-space-open-subspace], and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For $x\in|X|$ with image $b$, choose an etale scheme chart $U	o X$ and $u\in U$ above $x$. Put $U_b=U	imes_B\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)$, using residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] and spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $\widetilde u$ be the point of $U_b$ above $u$. Then $
u_f(x):=\dim_{\widetilde u}(U_b)$ is a finite nonnegative integer independent of the chart. Here dimension at a scheme point is the infimum of the topological Krull dimensions of its open neighbourhoods [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The function $
u_f:|X|	o\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ is locally constant. Its level sets are clopen subspaces $X_n$ and partition $X$. For every scheme morphism $h:B'	o B$, the pullback $f':X'=X	imes_BB'	o B'$ is smooth and $
u_{f'}(x')=
u_f(q(x'))$ for all $x'$, where $q:X'	o X$ is the projection; hence $X'_n=X_n	imes_BB'$. If $f$ is also separated and of finite presentation, then every nonempty geometric fibre of $X_n	o B$ is pure of topological Krull dimension $n$, meaning that all its irreducible components have dimension $n$. Separated means that the representable diagonal is a closed immersion on scheme tests, and finite presentation means local finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness; these last two mean, respectively, quasi-compact inverse images of affine scheme tests and a quasi-compact diagonal. A geometric fibre means base change along any morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega	o B$ with $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]; this includes an algebraic closure of a residue field.

proof.text: A smooth chart $U\to B$ is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type: its local finite presentation $R[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$ is in particular generated by the finitely many $t_i$. Thus the chartwise locally-finite-type hypothesis of [lem-sfb-space-local-fibre-dimension-open] holds. That node says that all affine charts at $x$ give the same finite nonnegative local fibre dimension. An arbitrary chart may be shrunk to an affine open $V\subseteq U$ around $u$; $V\to X$ is again an etale chart. After passing to the fibre, $V_b\to U_b$ is an open immersion, hence etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], so [lem-sfb-etale-topological-dimension-at-point] gives $\dim_{\widetilde u}V_b=\dim_{\widetilde u}U_b$. Consequently the value in the statement is defined for every chart and agrees with the function $\delta_f$ of that node.

source.place: Tag 04NM, definition-dimension-fibre; Tag 04NT, lemma-openness-bounded-dimension-fibres, chart-independence and finiteness

proof.text: For each etale scheme chart $a:U\to X$, its composite $g:U\to B$ is smooth by hypothesis. The equality proved in step 1 identifies $\nu_f\circ|a|$ with $u\mapsto\dim_{\widetilde u}U_{g(u)}$. This is locally constant by [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant]. Thus the inverse image of every level set, and of its complement, is open on every etale scheme chart. By the defining final topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], both sets are open on $|X|$. In particular $\nu_f$ is locally constant.

Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $p:U\to X$ and put $O_n=\{u:\nu_f(p(u))=n\}$, an open subscheme of $U$ by step 2. On $R=U\times_XU$ the two inverse images of $O_n$ agree because their images in $X$ agree. Apply [lem-trf-etale-open-chart-morphism-descent] with $Z=X$ and $q=p|_{O_n}$ to obtain the unique open subspace $X_n\subseteq X$ pulling back to $O_n$. Its point image is the level set by the atlas criterion in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Descend the complementary invariant open in the same way. These give disjoint complementary open subspaces, so $X_n$ is clopen. Every point has exactly one finite nonnegative value by step 1; the $X_n$ therefore partition $X$.

For $h:B'\to B$, the pulled-back atlas $U'=U\times_BB'\to X'=X\times_BB'$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Cover $U$ by the open loci where its smooth map to $B$ has constant fibre dimension $d$ (step 2 on the scheme chart). Each restriction is smooth, by precomposition with the etale open immersion [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties], and its fibres are open in those of $U$, so by [lem-sfb-etale-topological-dimension-at-point] it is smooth of relative dimension $d$ in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] its base change to $B'$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$; hence $U'\to B'$ is smooth. Smoothness is local on the source, including etale covers, by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. Indeed, for any other chart $V\to X'$, the scheme $V\times_{X'}U'$ surjects etale onto $V$, its map to $B'$ is smooth by precomposing the smooth $U'\to B'$ with an etale morphism, and smoothness descends to $V$. Thus $f'$ is smooth in precisely the chartwise sense of the statement.

source.place: Tag 01VB, lemma-base-change-smooth; Tag 02NK, lemma-base-change-relative-dimension-d; smoothness etale local on source and target

proof.text: Let $x'\in|X'|$ and choose $u'\in U'$ above it, using surjectivity of the pulled-back atlas. Write $u\in U$ for its image, $b'=f'(x')$ and $b=h(b')$. Apply [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] to the locally finite type scheme morphism $U\to B$, its base change $U'\to B'$, and $u'$. It identifies the fibre over $b'$ with the residue-field base change of the fibre over $b$, and gives equality of their dimensions at the indicated fibre points. By step 1, those two values are exactly $\nu_{f'}(x')$ and $\nu_f(q(x'))$. This proves the claimed pointwise base-change formula, including arbitrary transcendental residue-field extensions.

source.place: Tag 02FY, lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change (1); compare Tag 04NS (1) for spaces

proof.text: The point image of the open pullback $X_n\times_BB'\subseteq X'$ is $q^{-1}(|X_n|)$ by [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests]. By step 5 this is exactly the level set $\nu_{f'}^{-1}(n)$, the point image of $X'_n$. The order detection for open subspaces in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], applied in both directions, identifies the two open subfunctors. Therefore $X'_n=X_n\times_BB'$ as subspaces, not just as point sets.

Assume now the additional finite-presentation and separation hypotheses. Fix any $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$ as in the statement and put $Y=X_n\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The whole fibre $X_\Omega$ is quasi-compact by the scheme-test definition of quasi-compactness of $f$; its clopen subspace $Y$ is quasi-compact (adjoin the open complement to any covering). Its charts are locally of finite type since they are smooth by step 4. Its diagonal is quasi-compact: it is the restriction of the base change of the quasi-compact relative diagonal of $f$; on scheme tests apply [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], and restriction to these opens is base change of the diagonal to $Y\times_\Omega Y$. Thus $Y$ satisfies the finite-type and quasi-separated hypotheses of [lem-sfb-space-component-generic-chart-dimension]. For each irreducible component $C$ of a nonempty $Y$, that node supplies its generic point $\eta_C$ and gives $\dim C=\dim_u U$ for a chart point $u$ above $\eta_C$. By steps 5 and 6, every point of $Y$ has local fibre dimension $n$. A chart $U\to Y$ composed with the open immersion $Y\subseteq X_\Omega$ is an etale chart of $X_\Omega$, so by step 1 the value $n$ is computed on $U$ itself. Since the base is the spectrum of a field, the fibre of a chart $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is $U$ itself, so $\dim_u U=n$. Hence $\dim C=n$ for every $C$, proving the required purity.
